name: Infinite Filmstrip Gallery
summary: Vertical columns of media tiles crawl endlessly and seamlessly in opposing directions, forming a continuously moving mood-board wall. A rock-steady oversized headline holds the center while whole-board theme swaps recolor every cell at once — an ever-moving, ever-recoloring wall that never visibly repeats.

composition: Symmetric tri-column (or flanking-column) layout: infinite tile columns frame a centered typographic core that commands the negative space.
Tight tile grid with near-zero gutters builds density — the wall reads as ONE fabric, not discrete cards.
Dozens of small cells beat a few large ones: the mood-board effect needs mass.
layering: Two planes only: the moving tile wall behind, the static headline + CTA plate in front.
The wall stays lower-contrast than the front plate so the busy motion never wins the legibility fight.
Loops must be seamless — a visible seam or stutter destroys the infinite illusion.
lighting: Emissive-on-black: bright cells glow against a pure black field; the black itself is the vignette.
No shadows — flatness is correct here; the wall is a graphic surface, not a physical stack.
typography: Massive geometric sans headline in solid accent color, tightly stacked; a small tracked-out eyebrow above provides editorial framing.
On theme swap the headline crossfades to the new accent — type and imagery share one color story.

rules: Pure black base + exactly ONE saturated hue per theme, governing both the type and the curated imagery — each mood is one color story.
Theme swaps re-skin every cell at once; partial recolors read as errors.

easing: Constant-velocity LINEAR crawl for the columns — no easing at all; it must loop seamlessly.
The centered headline never moves; theme-accent crossfades are the only type motion.
pacing: Perpetual slow ambient scroll — background texture, never demanding attention.
Slow enough that any single tile can be glimpsed, fast enough that the wall visibly lives.
choreography: Adjacent columns crawl in OPPOSING directions (up vs down) — the counter-flow is what makes the wall feel alive and parallaxed.
Theme swaps hit all cells simultaneously while the headline crossfades its accent.

gapNotes: Textured tile planes in scrolling columns are expressible, but a seamless-loop column driver (wrap-around repositioning without a visible seam) does not exist as a primitive — hand-building it per instance is error-prone.
Whole-board theme swap needs a coordinated multi-node material/texture switch (a 'theme token' driver) — today each node would be edited individually.
Sourcing 30+ cohesive, single-hue-curated images per theme is a FLUX batch pipeline that exists ad hoc but is not productized.

whenToUse: Creative studios, galleries, media brands, and mood-board/showcase hubs where volume of work IS the message.
Backgrounds behind a hero when the brief wants density and life without interaction.
whenNotToUse: Interfaces needing readable, CLICKABLE individual media items — the perpetual crawl makes single tiles hard to target.
Sparse content (fewer than ~20 items) — the wall exposes thin catalogs.
Reduced-motion contexts: the crawl must pause to a static grid.

notes: The still center headline is structural — without it the counter-flowing wall has no anchor and reads as chaos.
Never combine with another perpetual-motion family; one ambient motion system per surface.

antiRepetition.notes: Same cluster as media-showreel-gallery and editorial-product-gallery — one gallery grammar per option set.

sources.title: Mood Board Infinite Filmstrip Media Gallery
sources.motionEvidence: Founder monitor session, live demo: opposing-direction column crawl observed over multiple loop cycles (seam checked); theme swap triggered — simultaneous whole-board recolor and headline accent crossfade captured from the sequence.
